title: Returning Supplement Premium Charged for Days Covered by Another Medicare Coverage
content:
A policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies pays nothing for any day on which a Medicare Advantage enrollment of the same member is still in force, so supplement premium charged for such a month buys the policyholder nothing and is returned to them as a correction of the rate charged.

The return is booked as a correction entry on the policy's premium account against the single premium charge it corrects. Once it is booked, the money is paid back to the policyholder by the way their premium reaches the plan, the amount is credited against what their premium account shows outstanding, and the new entry stands on the account alongside the charge it corrects, carrying the reason the correction was made.

## Booking the return

The correction is booked with `post_overlap_premium_return_c83152d2`, which is an agent-side tool: the representative unlocks it and then calls it. One call books one return against one named premium charge.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form it takes |
|---|---|---|
| `medigap_policy_id` | The reference number of the Medicare Supplement policy whose premium account is being corrected, read from the policyholder's policy record | An identifier |
| `customer_id` | The member reference number of the policyholder the premium is returned to, read from their member profile | An identifier |
| `source_premium_entry_id` | The reference number of the single premium charge this return corrects, read from the entries on that policy's premium account | An identifier |
| `billing_period` | The first month of the span whose premium is being returned | Written as YYYY-MM |
| `returned_months` | How many months of cover the returned premium paid for | A whole number of months, one of 1, 3, 6 or 12 |
| `return_amount` | The money handed back, in USD | Recorded to 2 decimal places and never negative |

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence in plain text naming the reference number of the new premium account entry, the policy it was booked on, the amount returned and the charge it corrects. Receiving that sentence is what says the return is on the account; no other value is returned.
